why:
Already renamed, and this is the deprecated alias still standing in the public surface. Issue 0330: `BoardConfig` is a core, RMW-AGNOSTIC trait, so it must not name a concrete backend -- a board with an XRCE agent or a Cyclone peer still has a locator and it was never a zenoh one. `locator()` is the live name; `zenoh_locator()` survives as a defaulted method that forwards to it, so an out-of-tree board crate that still spells the old name keeps compiling with a deprecation warning. Recorded rather than left implicit because a `#[deprecated]` item is still API a reader can find, and this one teaches a reader the wrong thing about what layer the trait belongs to. Same class as issue 0225; the deprecation dates from 0.6.0. `locator()` is at `packages/platform/nros-platform/src/board/config.rs:43`, the forwarder at :58.

REMOVAL IS DEFERRED, ON PURPOSE (recorded 2026-08-27, phase-379 W5). The previous text ended `its removal is the follow-up`, which reads as work this campaign owes. It is not. The maintainer's decision this week is that the tree's `#[deprecated]` items retire TOGETHER, as one batch on a version boundary -- and W5 is still ADDING forwarders under that policy (commit 92402ece0, the same week, gave all 25 `nros_param_*` C entry points `NROS_DEPRECATED_MSG` forwarders). Do not delete this method as parity work.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE SOURCE 2026-08-27, and the row was short by one forwarder and wrong about a second thing:

* A SECOND trait carries the same alias and has no row of its own: `ThreadxConfig::zenoh_locator` at `packages/boards/nros-board-common/src/threadx_config.rs:69`, `#[deprecated(since = "0.6.0")]` forwarding to `ThreadxConfig::locator` (:53). It produces no parity row because `nros-board-common` is not in the extracted Rust surface (the extractor walks the `nros` facade), so this row is the only place it is written down. Its alias is WEAKER than this one's: a defaulted method's OVERRIDE is no longer consulted, so an out-of-tree overlay that still overrides `zenoh_locator` is silently ignored rather than warned -- called out in that file's own docs.
* The five inherent `with_zenoh_locator()` builders (`nros-board-{mps2-an385,esp32-qemu,threadx-linux,freertos,threadx-qemu-riscv64}/src/config.rs`) are NOT an unreached rename. Each is a `#[deprecated(since = "0.6.0")]` forwarder to a `with_locator()` that landed with issue 0330: five more members of the same retire-later batch, unrowed for the same surface reason.
* The three `pub zenoh_locator: &'static str` struct FIELDS (`nros-board-{mps2-an385,esp32-qemu}/src/config.rs`, `nros-board-common/src/base_config.rs`) are the one part that genuinely still spells the backend -- and issue 0330 DECLINED to rename them in writing: "a much larger blast radius through struct literals, and the board layer is where naming a backend is legitimate. Remaining work, not a leak of the core API." That is a board-layer decision, not core-API leakage and not this campaign's work list. Recorded here, deliberately not fixed.
